samples.summary: replaceActive's new internal re-search can make the bar replace a different occurrence than the one highlighted to the user
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:80 pushes `state.matches` + `state.activeIndex` into `editor.setSearchMatches()`, and that highlighted set is what the user sees. With the diff, `replaceActive` (packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:63) re-runs `search()` against the *changed* document before replacing, and `search()` (find-replace.ts:29-31) deliberately keeps the previous numeric `activeIndex` whenever it is still in range. If the concurrent edit (local typing or a remote peer, see the `store.onRemoteChange` path referenced at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1564) added or removed an earlier occurrence, index N now names a different match than the one rendered as active, so the click at docs-find-bar.tsx:136 rewrites text the user never had highlighted. The out-of-diff consumer that assumed `matches[activeIndex]` was the painted match is docs-find-bar.tsx:80/136; nothing there re-syncs highlights before the write. Fix likely belongs in the new code (re-anchor the active match by position rather than by index).

samples.summary: Find bar clears `state.matches` directly on an invalid regex; the new unconditional `search()` inside replace ignores that and can throw out of the click handler
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:89-95 wraps `state.search(...)` in try/catch and, on a regex compile error, assigns `state.matches = []` / `state.activeIndex = -1` directly — i.e. the caller owns that field as an error state. The diff makes `replaceActive`/`replaceAll` call `this.search(this.query, this.options)` unconditionally (find-replace.ts:63, 86) *outside* that try/catch; `search()` stores the bad query before `doc.searchText` throws (find-replace.ts:24-26), so any path that reaches `state.replaceAll(...)` at docs-find-bar.tsx:145 with a stale invalid regex throws an unhandled exception through the React onClick. The `matchCount === 0` / `activeIndex < 0` guards at lines 134 and 143 appear to block this today, which is why this is minor rather than major, but the caller's hand-cleared `matches` no longer has any effect on replace behaviour.

samples.summary: Replace guards in the find bar now test stale state, so Replace/Replace All can silently no-op with the buttons still enabled
samples.evidence: docs-find-bar.tsx:134 (`state.activeIndex < 0`) and :143 (`state.matches.length === 0`), plus the `disabled={matchCount === 0}` buttons at :301/:308, are all evaluated against the pre-refresh state. After the diff, `replaceActive`/`replaceAll` re-search first and may find zero matches (the searched text was edited away), returning without any write; the click produces no change and no feedback until `syncHighlights()` at :137/:146 updates the counter. Contract note: the component's comments (:126-131) still describe replace as acting on the matches it last synced.

verdict.reason: Every cited location checks out. find-replace.ts:63 re-runs search() against the current document inside replaceActive, and search() at :29-31 re-binds the active match by ordinal index only (never by blockId/offset), then :66-67 replaces matches[activeIndex] from that fresh list. The consuming find bar paints highlights solely via editor.setSearchMatches(state.matches, state.activeIndex) at docs-find-bar.tsx:80, called only from runSearch (:96), handleNext/handlePrevious (:116/:123) and *after* the replace (:137); handleReplace (:132-139) does no pre-write re-sync and its guard reads the same stale snapshot. The staleness window is reachable: docs-view.tsx:418-447 (store.onRemoteChange) refreshes the Doc and re-renders without re-running the find search, and editor.ts:4047-4049/4206-4217 show searchMatches/activeMatchIndex only change via setSearchMatches or clearSearchMatches, so the editor keeps painting the old match list. An earlier occurrence added/removed by a remote peer or by local typing therefore makes index N name a different occurrence, and Replace writes to text the user never had highlighted — a wrong-target CRDT mutation (major). Lane fit is borderline with the correctness lens, but the violated assumption lives in a different package's consumer (docs-find-bar.tsx:80 vs :136), which falls under "violated invariant other modules assume" / "behaviour change to an exported symbol"; any residual doubt keeps the finding.
